newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Sibtorgbank shareholders to liquidate bank.
newsitem.headline: Russian Sibtorgbank shareholders to liquidate bank.

text.p: Shareholders of Sibirsky Torgovy Bank (Sibtorgbank), a medium-sized Russian bank, have decided to liquidate the bank following the revocation of its licence, a bank official said on Wednesday.
The official told Reuters a creditors' meeting on May 30 would appoint someone to head a liquidation commission at Sibtorgbank, one of the biggest banks in Siberia.
The Central Bank revoked Sibtorgbank's licence on April 21. It had been in difficulties for several months, and in August last year the Central Bank imposed a temporary administration on it.
On April 1 this year assets had fallen to 436.95 billion roubles ($75.8 million) from 626.99 billion a year earlier.
The number of Russian banks is shrinking because of tougher Central Bank regulation and falling inflation, which have put an end to easy trading profits.
Banks mushroomed in Russia after the start of economic reforms in 1992.
The Central Bank revoked about 30 banking licences this year and granted 11 licences to new banks. As of January 1, 1997 there were 2,603 banks in Russia.
